articles.title: Labour calls for M4 relief road, seven years after axing the plan
articles.summary: Seven years after the party axed the project, Labour says the Welsh government should build the road.
articles.body:
Labour's Welsh leader has called for the Plaid Cymru administration to start work on an M4 relief road - seven years after his party had axed it.

Ken Skates told BBC Wales that there was "no other option on the table" to solve congestion in Newport, and has backed a version of the original plan with changes.

The move will be seen by some as an attempt to distance Welsh Labour from part of the legacy of former First Minister Mark Drakeford.

Labour will table a vote in the Senedd on Wednesday calling for an "appropriate relief road" to be built.

A report said the road could now cost £3bn to build. Plaid Cymru accused Labour of hypocrisy.

Skates' announcement comes weeks after the Welsh government set out some options for tackling congestion , including proposals to close junctions in Newport.

It also means that all opposition groups - Reform, Labour and the Tories - are in favour of a relief road.

Drakeford axed previous proposals for an M4 Relief Road in 2019 - on the grounds of cost and the impact on the environment.

The Welsh government has also commissioned an 18-month project to assess possible "roads-based" solutions - although it has ruled out the black route.

A report published earlier in October set out a number of alternatives to a new motorway, and said the relief road could cost around £3bn.

It also warned that the route was no longer safeguarded through the planning system.

"Over time, new development or other land use changes may occur within parts of the former corridor, making it progressively more difficult or expensive to deliver the same highway alignment in the future," it said.

But Ken Skates said the report "shows that no single or combined solution will adequately alleviate congestion on the M4 around Newport.

"That means that there is no other option on the table other than a relief road if we wish to solve the problem of congestion on that route."

He said he believed that an amended version of the original black route - the proposed motorway south of Newport that had been examined and backed by a public inquiry in 2019 - should be the road that got built.

The Welsh Labour leader said the proposed blue route alternative - using existing roads in part - was not appropriate.

"In reality, the black route remains the only appropriate route," Skates said.

"Further work would have to be undertaken to make sure that all environmental concerns today are met and adequately responded to, but something has to be done about congestion."

Asked what he would say to accusations of a U-turn, Skates added: "Well, it's a world away from where we were in 2019.

"Back then, we had come out of the EU, Brexit was causing enormous concern, we were planning for a no deal.

"We were... almost a decade into austerity. There was simply not the sort of money that was required to build the black route available to the Welsh government.

"It was right not to go ahead with it at the time because of the financial cost. I do believe firmly that had we gone ahead with it, it would have been paused or cancelled during Covid."

Skates said he wanted to know from the Welsh government what the status was now of the protected route for the relief road - which was ditched after the scheme was axed.

In a debate on 29 September, Deputy Transport Minister Mark Hooper said the black route was not achievable.

"The protected route status went when it was cancelled," he said.

"So, we're talking about decades of work to even get that off the ground."

Skates spoke ahead of the Co-operative Movement conference on Saturday, where he will say that people in the region "should be trusted, empowered and respected in deciding what affects them".

"Their need for congestion to be dealt with can only realistically be met through getting to work on a relief road.

"The debate over an appropriate solution and the balancing of environmental, human and economic concerns should be led by the people of the region, who know best what is needed in and for their communities."

Local Plaid Cymru MS, Peredur Owen Griffiths, who represents Casnewydd Islwyn, said Labour's "hypocrisy is astounding".

"It's as if they've forgotten they were in government for 27 years and scrapped plans to address the issue of congestion in and around Newport - only to now U-turn in opposition," he said.

"Plaid Cymru is clear that doing nothing isn't an option... the action we're considering could reduce traffic by 10% in just four years," he said.

articles.title: Festa de Frei Galvão: conheça as pílulas e tradições do santo em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Tradições representam a fé dos devotos no primeiro santo nascido no Brasil e fazem parte das visitas ao santuário no interior de SP.
articles.summary: A Festa de Frei Galvão em Guaratinguetá celebra o primeiro santo brasileiro com ritos como as pílulas da fé e a porta da humildade no santuário paulista.
articles.body:
Fitas com três nós que simbolizam fé, esperança e caridade, pequenos papéis com orações que podem ser ingeridos e uma porta com pouco mais de um metro de altura, que exige uma reverência para ser atravessada.

Essas são as tradições que fazem parte da devoção a Frei Galvão, em Guaratinguetá , no interior de São Paulo.

Os símbolos estão presentes no santuário dedicado ao primeiro santo nascido no Brasil e fazem parte da experiência de fiéis que visitam o local para rezar, agradecer e fazer pedidos. A Festa de Frei Galvão começou nesta sexta-feira (16) e deve reunir cerca de 120 mil devotos ao longo de dez dias de programação.

Uma das tradições do santuário é amarrar fitas com três nós, cada um associado a um significado: fé, esperança e caridade. Durante a visita, os devotos são convidados a fazer os nós e deixar pedidos pessoais.

O costume é inspirado no cordão que Frei Galvão usava na roupa e que simbolizava seus votos religiosos. Hoje, as fitas coloridas representam uma forma de expressar a devoção ao santo. Entre os pedidos deixados pelos fiéis estão intenções relacionadas à família, à união e à fé.

Frei Galvão e pílulas de fé, em Guaratinguetá. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Outra tradição ligada ao santo são as chamadas pílulas de Frei Galvão. Os pequenos papéis comestíveis levam uma oração e são distribuídos aos fiéis no santuário.

A voluntária Elenice Paiva de Oliveira participa da distribuição e conta que costuma incentivar os devotos a tomar as pílulas com fé. Segundo ela, os relatos de quem retorna para compartilhar suas experiências são motivo de emoção.

“Eu falo para eles tomarem pílula com fé, depois vem trazer testemunho para a gente, porque a gente também se emociona com o testemunho de que está doente e depois com o testemunho que foi curado. E é muito gratificante estar aqui, eu amo estar aqui.”

Além das fitas e das pílulas, outro espaço chama a atenção de quem visita o santuário: a Porta da Humildade, que tem pouco mais de um metro de altura.

Para atravessá-la, os visitantes precisam se curvar diante de uma representação do Menino Jesus e de uma relíquia: uma pedra da Gruta do Nascimento de Jesus.

A professora aposentada Alzira Vieira descreve a visita como um retiro espiritual. Ela conta que procura observar os detalhes do local e ficou impressionada com a simplicidade representada pela passagem.

“Eu estou assim, deslumbrada, né? Porque é tão difícil a gente achar, e tanta humildade, tanto é que ele tem uma Porta da Humildade.”

A necessidade de se abaixar para passar pela porta também provoca reflexões entre os visitantes. Uma das devotas relatou ter sentido algo bom ao fazer o gesto.

Fitas com três nós, que representam fé, esperança e caridade, e a Porta da Humildade, em Guaratinguetá. — Foto: Reprodução/TV Vanguarda

Frei Galvão nasceu em Guaratinguetá, no século XVIII, e foi canonizado em 2007 pelo papa Bento XVI, tornando-se o primeiro santo nascido no Brasil.

A relação dos moradores da região e dos peregrinos com o religioso também aparece nos pequenos gestos de devoção, como amarrar fitas, deixar bilhetes aos pés da imagem e tomar as pílulas.

Segundo o reitor do Santuário de Frei Galvão, Diego Atalino de Melo, a origem regional do santo e sua proximidade com a população ajudam a explicar essa relação.

“Frei Galvão, até mesmo por ser um santo franciscano, santo aqui da nossa terra, ele inspira muita proximidade, ele inspira familiaridade. E com quem a gente é familiar, a gente deixa de lado as cerimônias, os ritos, as palavras bonitas e se relaciona de uma maneira muito próxima.”

Para o reitor, os pedidos e as pílulas são expressões dessa confiança.

“Então o bilhetinho deixado aos pés do santo é o jeito do povo dizer que acredita, que confia nele. A pílula que é ingerida é exatamente essa expressão de alguém que acredita. O santo também me dá um remédio.”

articles.title: Aberta licitação para reforma e ampliação do Terminal Central de Araucária | G1
articles.standfirst: Parceria com a Prefeitura, que elaborou o projeto, garantiu a viabilidade da obra.
articles.summary: Parceria com a Prefeitura, que elaborou o projeto, garantiu a viabilidade da obra.
articles.body:
A Agência de Assuntos Metropolitanos do Paraná (Amep), instituição vinculada ao Governo do Estado, divulgou no último dia 25 de setembro o aviso de licitação para reforma e ampliação do Terminal Central de Araucária. A publicação no Diário oficial do Estado abre prazo para empresas interessadas em assumir a obra tão aguardada pela comunidade de Araucária. Na parceria, a Prefeitura entrou com a elaboração do novo projeto, a cargo da equipe da Secretaria de Planejamento (SMPL).

O investimento do Estado pode chegar a quase R$ 26,5 milhões. O projeto elaborado pela Prefeitura prevê uma requalificação da estrutura atual, com implantação de nova cobertura e novos pisos, ampliação do número de plataformas, criação de espaços comerciais e construção de novos banheiros. O terminal também será totalmente adequado às normas de acessibilidade e segurança, garantindo melhores condições de circulação, embarque e atendimento aos passageiros.

Entre as melhorias previstas está ainda a instalação de uma usina de energia solar com 242 painéis fotovoltaicos, além de elevador, sistema de climatização, monitoramento por câmeras e bicicletários. A obra inclui ainda novos espaços de apoio operacional e de atendimento ao público, ampliando a estrutura disponível para trabalhadores e usuários do transporte coletivo.

articles.title: Por que tropas e veículos militares argentinos estão circulando no RS | G1
articles.standfirst: Treinamento ocorre em Santa Maria, Rosário do Sul e Faxinal do Soturno e encerra ciclo de três anos de atividades conjuntas entre os dois países.
articles.summary: Treinamento ocorre em Santa Maria, Rosário do Sul e Faxinal do Soturno e encerra ciclo de três anos de atividades conjuntas entre os dois países.
articles.body:
A circulação de tropas argentinas e de veículos militares pelas estradas da Região Central do Rio Grande do Sul tem uma explicação: cerca de 400 militares do país vizinho participam de um treinamento conjunto ao Exército Brasileiro .

O Exercício Combinado Arandu ocorre até este sábado (17) em Santa Maria , Rosário do Sul e Faxinal do Soturno e reúne, ao todo, cerca de 2,8 mil militares e 640 viaturas blindadas e operacionais .

Segundo o Comando Militar do Sul, a atividade tem caráter exclusivamente de treinamento e busca aprimorar a capacidade das forças dos dois países de atuarem juntas, a chamada interoperabilidade .

Além da preparação militar, o exercício pode ser percebido por quem circula pelas estradas da região. O Comando Militar do Sul avisa para a possibilidade de aumento do movimento de viaturas militares nas rodovias durante o treinamento e pede atenção redobrada aos motoristas e respeito às orientações das equipes de trânsito.

Exercício Combinado Arandu no RS — Foto: Imagens cedidas/ Comando Militar do Sul

O Arandu é uma atividade regular de cooperação entre os exércitos dos dois países e é organizado em ciclos de três anos. O atual começou em 2024 e termina justamente com as atividades em território gaúcho neste ano.

O planejamento foi estabelecido durante a XVI Conferência Bilateral dos Estados-Maiores Argentina–Brasil, em 2024. Desde então, foram realizadas reuniões de coordenação nos dois países e, em 2025, um exercício de simulação. A atividade em campo realizada em 2026 é a terceira e última etapa.

O ciclo anterior havia sido concluído em 2023. Além de melhorar a atuação conjunta, o exercício busca, segundo o Exército brasileiro, fortalecer os laços históricos de cooperação e amizade entre as duas instituições.

articles.title: Midterms EUA: democratas superam republicanos em arrecadação | G1
articles.standfirst: Mesmo com doação milionária de Elon Musk, candidatos democratas arrecadaram muito mais que seus rivais republicanos, por amplas margens, em disputas-chave das midterms, segundo relatórios da Comissão Federal Eleitoral.
articles.summary: Candidatos democratas arrecadaram muito mais que seus rivais republicanos, por amplas margens, em disputas-chave, segundo relatórios da Comissão Federal Eleitoral.
articles.body:
Os candidatos democratas arrecadaram muito mais dinheiro do que seus rivais republicanos, por amplas margens, em disputas-chave para o Congresso dos Estados Unidos .

Apesar de uma injeção de US$ 276 milhões - equivalente a R$ 1,39 bilhão - do magnata da tecnologia Elon Musk no Partido Republicano , os números apresentados pelos candidatos à Comissão Federal Eleitoral (FEC, na sigla em inglês), nesta quinta-feira (15), mostram uma clara vantagem para o partido de oposição.

Os Estados Unidos renovam sua Câmara de Representantes e um terço do Senado nas midterms - chamadas em português de eleições de meio de mandato -, no dia 3 de novembro.

Em seis estados considerados decisivos para o controle do Senado - Texas, Alasca, Ohio, Maine, Michigan e Iowa - os democratas arrecadaram entre três e seis vezes mais do que seus oponentes republicanos no trimestre de julho a setembro, segundo uma análise do Punchbowl News.

O democrata James Talarico, candidato no Texas, arrecadou, por exemplo, o recorde de US$ 64 milhões (R$ 323 bilhões), contra apenas US$ 10,2 milhões (R$ 51,5 milhões) da campanha do republicano Ken Paxton, que ainda obteve uma contribuição adicional de US$ 8,5 milhões de comitês conjuntos com outros candidatos.

Os democratas também superaram os republicanos em disputas cruciais pela Câmara de Representantes, com pelo menos 47 republicanos em exercício arrecadando menos do que seus rivais democratas ou independentes, contra apenas cerca de seis titulares democratas superados em arrecadação por republicanos.

Midterms - Eleitora preenche cédula de votação em Harrisburg, na Pensilvânia (EUA) — Foto: REUTERS/Mike Segar

O dinheiro arrecadado é usado para propagandas nos meios de comunicação tradicionais (emissoras de TV, rádios) e nas plataformas sociais durante essas últimas semanas decisivas da campanha eleitoral.

Os democratas fizeram da arrecadação junto a pequenos doadores seu lema oficial de campanha, em especial os candidatos socialistas que concorrem em distritos-chave, como Michigan ou Nova York. Mas os números demonstram que eles também receberam generosas contribuições de grandes doadores, como ocorreu em disputas eleitorais anteriores.

A candidata democrata à Presidência em 2024, Kamala Harris, gastou US$ 1,17 bilhão (R$ 5,93 bilhão) em sua campanha de pouco mais de 100 dias, após a desistência da candidatura do então presidente Joe Biden.

Trump, que gastou US$ 255 milhões (R$ 1,28 bilhão), porém, saiu vitorioso. O cenário foi semelhante ao que ocorreu em 2016, frente à então candidata democrata Hillary Clinton, que também contou com aportes de grandes doadores.

articles.title: Baixa umidade na Paraíba: Inmet renova alerta para 161 cidades | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com o órgão, os municípios sob alerta podem registrar umidade relativa do ar entre 30% e 20% até o fim do dia.
articles.summary: Com índices entre 20% e 30%, o Inmet recomenda hidratação e cautela com o sol forte nos municípios afetados pela baixa umidade na Paraíba.
articles.body:
Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário dos Pretos, em Areia, Paraíba — Foto: Divulgação/Destino Brejo Paraíba

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) renovou, nesta sexta-feira (16), um alerta amarelo de baixa umidade do ar para 161 municípios da Paraíba. O período de aviso começou na quinta-feira (15) e agora segue até o fim desta sexta (16). Veja lista de municípios afetados abaixo.

Durante o período do alerta, a umidade relativa do ar deve variar entre 30% e 20%, índices considerados abaixo do recomendado para a saúde.

Segundo o Inmet, há baixo risco de incêndios florestais e de impactos à saúde, mas a população deve adotar medidas de prevenção para reduzir os efeitos do tempo seco.

evite atividades físicas intensas nos horários mais quentes;

procure permanecer em locais protegidos do sol entre o fim da manhã e a tarde.

Em caso de emergência, a população pode acionar a Defesa Civil, pelo telefone 199, ou o Corpo de Bombeiros, pelo telefone 193.

Alerta amarelo de baixa umidade do ar para a Paraíba — Foto: Reprodução Inmet.

articles.title: Prefeita de Bauru exonera marido após prisão em operação do Gaeco | G1
articles.standfirst: Renato Purini foi preso na manhã desta sexta-feira (16) no condomínio de alto padrão onde mora com Suéllen Rosim. Prisão é um desdobramento da Operação Cavalo de Troia que investiga fraude em licitação bilionária do lixo.
articles.summary: Renato Purini foi preso na Operação Cavalo de Troia por fraude em licitação de R$ 5,2 bilhões. A prefeita de Bauru, Suéllen Rosim, exonerou o marido do cargo.
articles.body:
A prefeita de Bauru (SP), Suéllen Rosim ( PSD ) exonerou o marido, Renato Purini, do cargo de secretário de governo após a prisão dele na manhã desta sexta-feira (16) . A prisão é um desdobramento da Operação Cavalo de Troia do Grupo Especial de Atuação contra o Crime Organizado (Gaeco) deflagrada em setembro.

O decreto com a exoneração de Purini foi publicado nesta sexta-feira em uma edição extraordinária do Diário Oficial de Bauru, assinada pela prefeita, que não chegou a ir pessoalmente à prefeitura nesta manhã.

Purini foi preso no condomínio de alto padrão onde mora com Suéllen Rosim e depois foi junto com a equipe do Gaeco que cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão na sala dele na prefeitura.

O ex-secretário de Governo Renato Purini, marido da prefeita de Bauru (SP), Suéllen Rosim (PSD), foi preso na manhã desta sexta-feira (16) durante operação deflagrada pelo Gaeco — Foto: Redes Sociais/Reprodução

Após o cumprimento dos mandados, o ex-secretário foi levado para Central de Polícia Judiciária e teve a prisão preventiva confirmada em audiência de custódia. Ele foi encaminhado para o Centro de Detenção Provisória de Bauru.

Renato Purini foi levado para a Prefeitura de Bauru durante ação do Gaeco nesta sexta-feira (16) — Foto: Carlos Torrente/TV TEM

No início da manhã, os servidores e funcionários foram impedidos de entrar no prédio da prefeitura, mas após a saída da equipe, foi permitida a entrada de todos que retomaram os trabalhos normalmente.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Bauru disse que, "desde o início das investigações conduzidas pelo Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (GAECO), tem colaborado integralmente com as autoridades, fornecendo documentos, informações e os esclarecimentos solicitados, e seguirá contribuindo com tudo o que for necessário para o avanço das apurações."

O texto informa também que "diante das informações tornadas públicas e das medidas em curso, o secretário municipal de Governo, Renato Purini, foi exonerado do cargo."

Em nota, o Ministério Público informou que além da prisão, houve cumprimento de mandados de busca e apreensão em endereços localizados não só na cidade do interior paulista, mas também na capital.

A investigação mira um suposto esquema criminoso relacionado à estruturação e à condução da concessão dos serviços de resíduos sólidos em Bauru, envolvendo contrato estimado em aproximadamente R$ 5,2 bilhões, com duração prevista de 30 anos, além de possíveis ajustes com vereadores.

Vídeo mostra momento em que secretário e marido da prefeita de Bauru (SP) é levado durante operação contra fraudes em licitação — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A nova fase da Cavalo de Troia decorre da evolução na análise de provas obtidas durante sua primeira etapa, especialmente das mensagens extraídas de aparelhos celulares apreendidos. Elas revelaram indícios da participação de outros agentes públicos e particulares nas práticas investigadas.

As investigações prosseguem, inclusive para a apuração de outros possíveis delitos e a identificação de eventuais participantes ainda não alcançados pelas medidas judiciais.

Marido da prefeita de Bauru e secretário, Renato Purini é preso em casa durante operação do Gaeco — Foto: TV TEM

As investigações do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado do Ministério Público começaram em março a partir de denúncias de ameaças contra catadores de materiais recicláveis da Ascam.

Segundo as apurações, Valdomiro Pereira da Silva Filho, marido da então presidente da Ascam, tinha ligação com uma facção criminosa e usava a influência para intimidar os trabalhadores da Associação dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis, que mantinha contratos de mais de R$ 5 milhões com a Prefeitura de Bauru com dispensa de licitação.

A partir do monitoramento de ligações de Valdomiro e da esposa dele, Gisele Moretti, presidente da associação, o Ministério Público descobriu que o casal também articulava esquemas para pedir propinas e interferir na licitação da gestão do lixo na cidade.

A interceptação das conversas revelou a participação de secretários municipais e executivos de empresas , o que levou à deflagração de duas operações paralelas promovidas pelo Gaeco com o apoio da Polícia Militar.

A ação cumpriu mandados de busca e apreensão e resultou na prisão temporária de sete pessoas em fases anteriores, duas delas, presas na Operação Mobius, já foram liberadas. As demais, presas na Operação Cavalo de Troia, permanecem presas, uma delas em prisão domiciliar. São elas:

Cilene Chabuh Bordezan : ex-secretária municipal de Meio Ambiente;

Vitor João de Freitas Costa : ex-secretário municipal de Negócios Jurídicos;

Sara Moura de Jesus : ex-secretária-adjunta de Meio Ambiente;

Hamilton Libório Agle: proprietário e CEO da empresa Estre Ambiental;

Talita de Andrade Soares Chieregatti : funcionária da Estre Ambiental (em prisão domiciliar).

Gisele Moretti, ex- presidente da Associação dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis (Ascam); e Valdomiro Pereira da Silva Filho, empresário e marido de Gisele Moretti, foram liberados.

Associação dos Catadores de Materiais Recicláveis (Ascam) em Bauru (SP) — Foto: Divulgação

A Operação Cavalo de Troia investiga o esquema para fraudar a licitação da concessão do sistema de gestão de resíduos sólidos urbanos de Bauru, projetada para durar 30 anos e a valiada em R$ 5,2 bilhões, o maior contrato da história do município.

A apuração aponta que o grupo atuava para direcionar as regras do edital a favor da empresa Estre Ambiental por meio de pessoas infiltradas na administração municipal.

Segundo o Ministério Público, a então secretária de Meio Ambiente, Cilene Bordezan, mantinha um relacionamento amoroso com o CEO da empresa, Hamilton Libório Agle, o que permitia que a concessionária elaborasse documentos e pareceres oficiais de dentro do próprio governo.

Gaeco aponta relação entre ex-secretária Cilene Bordezan e CEO Hamilton Libório Agle — Foto: Reprodução

Um dos presos conseguiu prisão domiciliar

A funcionária da Estre, Talita Andrade, acusada de ser uma das envolvidos na organização criminosa montada para fraudar a concessão do lixo de Bauru, deixou a penitenciária e está cumprindo prisão domiciliar.

A mudança foi comunicada na quinta-feira (15) pela Secretaria da Administração Penitenciária (SAP). A acusada deixou a penitenciária feminina Sant´Ana no dia de outubro, após decisão da Justiça.

Ela tinha sido transferida para a unidade no final de setembro, depois que teve a prisão convertida em preventiva. A defesa de Talita já vinha pedindo a prisão domiciliar por causa de uma doença da acusada e também pelo sofrimento da filha.

A TV TEM questionou a SAP sobre os outros quatro presos que, até a última atualização, estavam detidos em unidades prisionais. Já o ex-consultor da Fipe, Mário Luiz, estava foragido.

articles.title: Aulas são suspensas após árvore cair sobre escola em Campinas | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a direção da unidade, os alunos atingidos serão realocados para outras salas e todo o conteúdo será reposto. O prédio passará por reparos estruturais e as aulas serão retomadas na segunda-feira (19).
articles.summary: Segundo a direção da unidade, alunos serão realocados para outras salas e o conteúdo será reposto. O prédio passará por reparos e as aulas serão retomadas na segunda (19).
articles.body:
Uma árvore de grande porte caiu sobre a Escola Estadual Carlos Araújo Pimentel na madrugada desta terça-feira (13), no Jardim Santa Genebra, em Campinas (SP). Por conta dos estragos, as aulas foram suspensas e serão retomadas apenas na segunda-feira (19).

Ninguém ficou ferido e a direção informou que todo o conteúdo será reposto. Nesta sexta-feira (16), uma reunião de pais vai ocorrer normalmente em uma área não afetada do prédio.

Segundo a Unidade Regional de Ensino (URE) Campinas Leste, a queda foi provocada pelas fortes chuvas na região. A árvore atingiu parte do telhado do refeitório e de duas salas de aula.

Imagens enviadas à EPTV , afiliada da TV Globo , mostraram a raiz da árvore arrancada do solo e os galhos e parte do tronco atravessando o telhado.

A escola atende crianças dos anos iniciais do ensino fundamental e, de acordo com a autora do vídeo, os espaços danificados são usados por turmas do 1º, 2º e 3º ano. Por isso, parte do prédio continua interditada.

"Danificou bem a sala da minha filha [...] O material, inclusive das crianças, de estudo, está todo lá [...] Porque assim, ainda está caindo telha, as salas estão descobertas, entendeu? Então assim, é um risco também até para as nossas crianças e para os funcionários que estão trabalhando aqui", disse Eliane Oliveira, mãe de uma aluna.

Também mãe de um aluno, Cláudia Cardinalli disse ter medo de que algo aconteça com o filho. "Está dentro de uma escola que está com o problema de uma árvore no teto", comentou.

De acordo com a Secretaria de Educação (Seduc), os alunos cujas salas foram danificadas serão realocados para outros ambientes .

A Prefeitura de Campinas foi acionada para remover a árvore. Equipes da Fundação para o Desenvolvimento da Educação (FDE) e do Serviço de Obras e Manutenção Escolar (Seom) vistoriaram o local para organizar os reparos na estrutura.

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: Justiça proíbe entrega de título em Salvador | G1
articles.standfirst: Cerimônia estava marcada para este sábado (17). Decisão liminar prevê multa de R$ 500 mil em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: A Justiça da Bahia suspendeu a entrega do título de cidadão soteropolitano a Flávio Bolsonaro no Farol da Barra por risco de uso eleitoral e custos elevados.
articles.body:
Justiça proíbe entrega de título de cidadão soteropolitano a Flávio Bolsonaro no Farol da Barra — Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado

A decisão liminar foi assinada nesta sexta-feira (16) pela juíza Carla Graziela Costantino de Araújo, da 5ª Vara da Fazenda Pública, e prevê multa de R$ 500 mil em caso de descumprimento.

A magistrada também suspendeu a transferência temporária da sede do Legislativo municipal para o ponto turístico. A medida foi tomada em uma ação popular movida pela aposentada Maria Lúcia Andrade da Silva e tem cumprimento imediato.

Na decisão, a juíza apontou que a realização da solenidade e a mudança excepcional da sede da Câmara, durante a campanha do segundo turno das eleições, poderiam interferir na disputa eleitoral e dar à homenagem oficial um caráter promocional ou partidário em favor de um candidato à Presidência da República.

Com a decisão, a cerimônia prevista para este sábado está suspensa, assim como a transferência temporária da sede do Legislativo municipal para o local. A ordem determina a intimação urgente do presidente da Câmara e dos procuradores legislativos, por meio de oficial de Justiça de plantão e do sistema eletrônico.

Por que a Justiça suspendeu a cerimônia?

A juíza considerou que a escolha da data e do local para a solenidade poderia comprometer a imparcialidade da atuação institucional do Legislativo municipal no período eleitoral.

Outro ponto destacado foi o custo da transferência temporária da sede da Câmara para o Farol da Barra. Segundo a decisão, a mudança exigiria uma estrutura excepcional de servidores, segurança, cerimonial e equipamentos móveis, com despesas consideradas desproporcionais e desnecessárias.

A magistrada citou os princípios da economicidade e da razoabilidade ao fundamentar a suspensão.

Na ação, a autora também questionou a concessão da honraria e argumentou que Flávio Bolsonaro não teria prestado serviços relevantes ao município de Salvador.

O Título de Cidadão da Cidade do Salvador foi concedido ao senador por meio da Resolução nº 3.592/2026, aprovada em sessão plenária da Câmara Municipal em maio deste ano.

Flávio Bolsonaro foi o segundo candidato à Presidência da República mais votado em Salvador , com 391.188 votos. Ele ficou atrás do presidente Lula ( PT ), que recebeu mais que o dobro dos votos na capital baiana, 944.358.

Enquanto no âmbito geral da eleição, Flávio Bolsonaro saiu à frente — 47,03% dos votos ante os 45,16% de Lula —, na Bahia, ele conseguiu ampliar a votação obtida pelo pai , Jair Bolsonaro ( PL ), há quatro anos.

O senador recebeu 28,53% dos votos válidos no estado, na votação de domingo (4), contra 66,17% do atual presidente. Já Jair acumulou 24,31% dos votos no primeiro turno de 2022, contra 69,73% de Lula.

O senador superou Lula em apenas quatro cidades baianas no primeiro turno da eleição: Luís Eduardo Magalhães , na região oeste, Buerarema , no sul, Teixeira de Freitas e Itamaraju , ambas no extremo sul. Ao g1 , cientistas políticos apontaram que o fortalecimento do bolsonarismo no estado está ligado a conflitos agrários e às afinidades culturais e geográficas entre as cidades baianas e outras regiões do Brasil .

articles.title: Palestinians, US journalist attacked in West Bank pogrom: What we know
articles.summary: Israeli settlers attacked Palestinians harvesting olives and severely beat Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine.
articles.body:
Israeli settlers brutally attacked Palestinian olive pickers and a photojournalist working for The Washington Post in the occupied West Bank on Friday, beating villagers and setting olive groves ablaze.

The attack was among several targeting Palestinians trying to gather their olive harvest, with further assaults and arson reported in nearby communities as well.

These incidents are just the latest in weeks of intensifying pogroms on local communities in the West Bank by Israelis from illegal settlements who are largely protected – or at least unrestricted – by Israeli forces.

Veteran journalist Heidi Levine, 64, was taken to hospital after the assault on Friday in Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah. A Palestinian man was also shot in the thigh by Israeli soldiers, according to a witness who spoke to Al Jazeera and the Palestinian news agency Wafa.

Dozens of masked settlers attacked Palestinian farmers harvesting olives, throwing stones, using slingshots and setting trees on fire.

Levine, an American freelance photojournalist who works for The Washington Post, fell to the ground during the attack before she was set upon, witnesses said. “We looked and saw that there was a journalist … on the ground with people surrounding her, beating her, clubbing her, robbing her, pulling her up, beating her again and kicking her,” Jasper Nathaniel, an independent journalist who witnessed the attack, told Al Jazeera.

Levine later told reporters that her attackers “just kept kicking me and kicking me, like probably 50 times”.

Levine was wearing a protective vest marked “PRESS” on the front and back. Her cameras and phone were taken from her during the assault, the Washington Post reported.

Nathaniel said he and others managed to reach her when the settlers briefly backed away, but she struggled to stand. “She was in very, very bad shape. She couldn’t really get up off the ground,” he said.

As they helped her towards paramedics, settlers charged again, throwing more stones, he added. Levine was eventually taken to hospital in Ramallah.

Nathaniel said Israeli soldiers arrived after the settler assault and opened fire and used tear gas against Palestinians, shooting a man in the leg. “They do nothing to stop the settlers, and they speed into town and start firing their guns and tear-gassing, and they shoot a Palestinian man in the leg,” he said.

“They’re pointing their guns at the paramedics who are helping him, shoving journalists, including myself,” Nathaniel said, adding that the man was eventually taken away in an ambulance.

“We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities,” Matt Murray, executive editor of The Washington Post, said in a statement.

Wafa also reported that Israeli forces fired live ammunition and tear gas at Palestinians during the attack. After the soldiers left, Palestinians returned to harvesting their olives, Nathaniel added.

Where else have olive pickers been attacked?

There was violence in other parts of the occupied West Bank on Friday, as well. In Burqa, east of Ramallah, four Palestinians were reported to have been injured in a settler attack on olive pickers. In nearby Turmus Aya, settlers assaulted farmers and burned vehicles and olive trees. A civil defence volunteer was also injured, according to Wafa.

The attacks follow the killing of Ali Hassan Yasser al-Bazzari, 44, during an assault on Palestinians gathering olives near Burqa, northwest of Nablus, on October 7. Witnesses reported that settlers and Israeli soldiers attacked the harvesters.

Journalists documenting the violence have also been targeted. On October 6, armed settlers beat Palestinian AFP photographer Jaafar Ashtiyeh, 58, with rifle butts near Aqraba, south of Nablus. He was taken to hospital with injuries to his head and torso, according to witnesses, relatives and colleagues.

The Israeli settler pogroms have been going on for many weeks, and have stepped up as the seasonal Palestinian olive harvest gets under way.

The Israeli rights group Yesh Din has recorded at least 170 pogroms since September 27, around the start of the annual olive harvest, Reuters reported.

The violence threatens Palestinian livelihoods and access to their land. Farmers endure assaults, the destruction of trees and the theft of crops, while settlers have also begun stealing olives from Palestinian-owned groves themselves.

Al Jazeera correspondent Tareq Abu Azzoum reported that the intimidation extends beyond agricultural land to Palestinian homes and vehicles, creating pressure on communities to leave.

“People there are still living under threat of attack, not just on their agricultural lands, but also on their properties,” he said.

“Vehicles and houses have been repeatedly hit by settler attacks, which have been used by the Israeli military, apparently, to create a deterrent environment with Palestinians expected to leave these areas so they can later turn them into Israeli settlements.”

articles.title: UN warns Russian attacks and winter hardship could displace more Ukrainians
articles.summary: Millions of Ukrainians are preparing for another difficult winter as attacks on essential infrastructure, damaged homes and escalating living costs
articles.body: Millions of Ukrainians are preparing for another difficult winter as attacks on essential infrastructure, damaged homes and escalating living costs increase the risk of further displacement, the United Nations migration agency warned on Friday.With temperatures expected to drop in the coming months, families across the war-torn country are struggling to ensure access to dependable heating, electricity and water after years of conflict, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) said.The warning comes after Russian missiles and drones targeted Ukrainian cities this week, amid concerns that the United States could reduce intelligence sharing and military assistance to Kyiv, according to the Reuters.“Winter is fast approaching in Ukraine, and for many Ukrainians, the months ahead could be the most difficult since the full-scale war began,” Dejan Keserovic, IOM deputy chief of mission in Ukraine, told reporters in Geneva via a video link from Kyiv.Millions remain displaced as winter approachesAccording to the IOM's latest figures, nearly 3.6 million people remain internally displaced within Ukraine following Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. An estimated 3.8 million people have returned to their homes after being displaced, with many finding their properties damaged or partially destroyed.The agency said people who returned home within the past three months were the most likely to express an intention to leave again, highlighting growing anxiety over deteriorating living conditions.Meanwhile, European countries, including Poland, Germany and the Czech Republic, are currently hosting approximately six million Ukrainian refugees.Keserovic said host countries were expected to prepare for the possibility of another influx of Ukrainians if conditions in their homeland worsened.Russian attacks strain electricity, heating and water suppliesRepeated Russian strikes on energy facilities and other critical infrastructure have placed Ukraine's electricity, heating and water networks under increasing pressure, the IOM said.Missile and drone attacks have also continued to kill and injure civilians across the country, adding to the challenges faced by communities already struggling with the effects of prolonged warfare.Access to reliable water supplies has emerged as a particular concern because water infrastructure depends heavily on electricity to function.The IOM said it had installed 31 solar power stations to help keep water systems operational in different parts of Ukraine. However, the agency cautioned that the scale of humanitarian needs remained substantial.Funding shortfall threatens winter relief effortsThe UN agency also warned that a shortage of funding could undermine preparations for the approaching winter.Less than 7% of the IOM's Ukraine response plan for 2026 had received funding so far, leaving a significant gap between available resources and the assistance required.The agency stressed the urgent need for additional financial support to improve home insulation and help households withstand freezing temperatures.With damaged housing, unreliable utilities and rising living costs compounding the effects of the war, humanitarian agencies face mounting pressure to ensure vulnerable families can remain safe and warm during the coming months.You use AI every day. articles.title: Mom of 5th-grade student recalls terrifying moment son texted her about deadly shooting at Oregon elementary school
articles.summary: The mother of a fifth-grade student at Silver Rail Elementary School recalled the terrifying moment she received a text message from her son saying that there had been a shooting.
articles.body: The mother of a fifth-grade student at Silver Rail Elementary School recalled the terrifying moment she received a text message from her son saying that there had been a shooting. “Mom there was a school shooting we’re ok tho,” the message read. “I instantly turned to social media, and it was blasted all over,” Jenn Johnston told NBC News. About 20 minutes earlier, Johnston said she had received an automated phone call and text from the Bend, Oregon, school telling her that there was a lockdown in place. Follow live updates here After receiving the text from her son, she and her husband jumped into the car and drove to the school. Johnston said parents were rerouted to a nearby church, where they waited for hours with few updates from police and school officials. It wasn’t until about 6 p.m. when her tearful son jumped off the school bus and ran into her arms. “The kids were bused from the school to the church and were released to parents from youngest to oldest,” Johnston said. “My son, being in fifth grade, was the very last class to be released.” The shooting happened around 1 p.m. local time Thursday after a suspected teenager armed with a long gun gained entry to the school by firing through the locked doors. A teacher and three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, were killed. Two other people, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were critically injured. The suspect was said to be a 16-year-old Bend resident. He was shot and killed by a good Samaritan who pursued him, authorities said. Justin Penfield said he and his wife were together when they received a notification from the school. A friend who was already at the school told them to get to the building quickly, he said. Penfield recalled seeing a “massive police presence” and finding his son’s kindergarten class already outside. Penfield said that, as he walked his son back to their car, he saw a man standing next to a pickup truck with “seven or eight gunshot holes in his truck.” According to Penfield, the man told him he was driving back from lunch when he saw someone throw what appeared to be a shotgun over the fence and then jump into the school’s playground. The man said he yelled to ask the guy what he was doing because he thought it was odd, Penfield said, recounting his conversation with the man. According to Penfield, the man told him the gunman turned and opened fire on his truck. Penfield said the man told him he sped away and called 911. Mindy Miranda said her 8-year-old daughter was in her third-grade classroom upstairs when shots rang out. She said they are trying to process what happened “as a family and as a community.” “I never in a thousand years thought it would be at Silver Rail Elementary, a place that I safely drop our daughter off at every day, and she goes to learn and to thrive and to be a part of a great group of people there,” she said. Bend Mayor Melanie Kebler said at a vigil Thursday evening that the shooting was a dark day for the city and “there are simply no words for the loss that we have suffered.”

articles.title: Ethiopia announces instalment of interim government in Tigray
articles.summary: After military pushed back TPLF uprising, PM Abiy Ahmed promises free elections within six months.
articles.body:
Ethiopia has announced that an interim government will take control of the state of Tigray, after its armed forces retook control of the northern region.

The installation of the six-month administration was announced in a statement by Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on Friday. He pledged that free elections would then be held in the state.

The move comes after the Ethiopian military pushed back an uprising launched last month by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Tigray’s main political party had launched the insurrection after announcing in April that it was retaking control of the region, effectively ending a peace deal with Ethiopia’s federal government.

The government promised that the interim government would create “a stable political situation” in Tigray so that free elections could be held. It has appointed five officials to run the state, including the mayor of the capital, Mekelle.

The officials will carry out “directives and instructions” delivered directly from the federal government.

The TPLF has yet to respond to the announcement. The rebel group launched an ambitious offensive in September in alliance with several other armed groups aimed at toppling the Abiy government. The Ethiopian government has accused the breakaway state of Eritrea of supporting the TPLF, accusations that Eritrea has denied.

After some early gains in the Afar region, its fighters were defeated and lost Tigray’s major cities. They surrendered in Mekelle in early October. Eritrean troops who had entered Tigray withdrew after heavy drone strikes from the Ethiopian armed forces.

The TPLF governed Ethiopia for nearly 30 years until 2018, when Abiy’s party came to power. Tigray, in response, boycotted national elections and rejected the central government, creating a severe rift.

The region remains scarred by the 2020-2022 war between federal forces, backed at that time by Eritrea, and the TPLF, which resulted in the killing of almost 600,000 people.

A peace deal ended the fighting, but key promises were not kept, including the return of displaced people and the disarmament of the TPLF.

Since the recent escalation, Ethiopia and Eritrea have accused each other of inciting war, raising fears of a wider conflict.

On Wednesday, the United States urged both sides to “de-escalate” during a phone call between Abiy and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

articles.title: Can Russia help ease tensions between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
articles.summary: Russia has close ties with the Taliban and is courting Islamabad, but analysts say its leverage remains uncertain.
articles.body:
Islamabad, Pakistan – Sitting with his elbows on his knees, Russia’s Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev leaned towards Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, for talks in Rawalpindi on October 14.

While Kolokoltsev was in Pakistan, Sergey Naryshkin, director of Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), flew into Kabul to meet the Taliban’s intelligence chief, Abdul Haq Wasiq.

Officially, Russia, Pakistan and Afghanistan have issued little beyond standard statements about the meetings. But the signs are clear: Pakistan and Afghanistan have spent the past year exchanging fire and public threats. Qatar and Turkiye brokered a ceasefire in Doha last October and China hosted talks in Urumqi in April, but attacks inside Pakistan continued. Islamabad again struck Afghan territory in June, September and this month.

Russia now appears to be stepping in as a mediator.

Moscow’s special representative for Afghanistan, Zamir Kabulov, told Russia’s TASS news agency earlier this month that his country was ready to play peace broker between Kabul and Islamabad if both sides requested it.

Pakistan’s ambassador to Russia, Faisal Niaz Tirmizi, said in March that Islamabad had approached Moscow. The Taliban, though, have not publicly requested Russian mediation, raising questions about how much and in what capacity Moscow can push Pakistan and Afghanistan to talks when other mediators have struggled.

A complicated history adds to the challenge Russia faces.

Pakistan’s military media wing, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), said the Rawalpindi meeting discussed issues of “mutual interest and the regional security environment, with particular emphasis on strengthening bilateral security cooperation.”

The statement did not mention Afghanistan and neither Russian officials nor the Taliban have disclosed what the intelligence chiefs discussed. Moscow has, however, voiced concern about the fighting.

“We are seriously concerned about the ongoing military confrontation between Pakistan and Afghanistan, which affects civilians, including children,” the Russian embassy in Kabul posted on X earlier this month.

The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) said Pakistani strikes between September 30 and October 1 killed at least 10 civilians , mostly children.

In decades past, the idea of Russia mediating between Pakistan and the Taliban might have been unthinkable. Throughout the Cold War and even after the collapse of the Soviet Union, Russia was – and remains in many ways – one of the closest strategic and military partners of India, the neighbour Pakistan has fought multiple wars against. While in Afghanistan, Russia backed the Northern Alliance against the Taliban throughout the 1990s.

But in recent years, Russia has significantly strengthened relations with both Pakistan and the Taliban. Then Pakistani Prime Minister Imran Khan was in Moscow when Russian forces invaded Ukraine in 2022. Last year, Russia became the first country in the world to officially recognise the Taliban government in Afghanistan.

Those shifts have been driven by Russia’s desire to broaden its options in South Asia, at a time when India has embraced the United States and to counter the rise of the Afghan branch of ISIL, also known as the Islamic State in Khorasan Province or ISKP. While the Taliban are concerned with ruling Afghanistan, ISKP has broader territorial ambitions and carried out an attack in Moscow in 2024 that killed nearly 150 people. The Taliban and the ISKP are sworn enemies.

Fighting between Pakistan and the Taliban created regional instability and Moscow was worried that could make it easier for armed groups to spill into Central Asia, said Taimur Khan, a research associate at the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad (ISSI).

“Mediation also helps Moscow preserve its regional influence and avoid a vacuum that could invite renewed extra-regional involvement,” he told Al Jazeera.

Qatar and Turkiye brokered a ceasefire between Pakistan and the Taliban in Doha last October, but talks in Istanbul collapsed the following month and skirmishes resumed. Islamabad also launched air raids inside Afghanistan. China hosted talks in Urumqi in April.

In mid-September, Turkiye’s intelligence chief, Ibrahim Kalin, met Taliban officials in Kabul and Kandahar before travelling to Islamabad.

An attack in Kohat followed on September 18, with Pakistan striking Afghanistan on September 24 and October 1.

“Other actors have so far achieved more tangible mediation results in this conflict,” Eldaniz Gusseinov, a Central Asia analyst and head of research at the geopolitical foresight agency, Nightingale Int, told Al Jazeera.

Russia’s own effort stalled at a Moscow meeting on October 5.

Kabulov told TASS that the Afghan delegation objected to Afghanistan being mentioned too often in connection with “terrorism”.

“For Pakistan, this is a substantive security issue, not merely a matter of wording,” Pakistan’s Foreign Office spokesperson, Sajjad Haider Khan, said on October 9 at a weekly media briefing.

Kabul-based security analyst Tameem Bahiss said the objection reflected Kabul’s longstanding position.

“Accepting language that repeatedly associates Afghanistan with terrorism could be seen as an acknowledgement of the very allegations Kabul has consistently denied,” he told Al Jazeera.

At the Moscow meeting, Pakistan’s special representative for Afghanistan, Mohammad Sadiq, said “terrorism” remained at the core of Afghanistan’s problems.

Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi said the two countries’ problems could be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, according to Afghan media.

Pakistan says the Pakistani Taliban and other armed groups shelter in Afghanistan.

Kabul rejects the allegation, saying it does not allow its territory to be used against other countries and that Pakistan’s security problems are largely internal, Bahiss said.

Moscow’s public warnings have focused on the ISKP.

“There is no visible public pressure from Russia on the Taliban over Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), and Moscow is unlikely to exert such pressure,” Gusseinov said. TTP is the official name of the Pakistani Taliban, which is behind dozens of the deadliest attacks Pakistan has suffered in recent years.

He argued that pressing the Taliban hard on Pakistan’s behalf would undermine Moscow’s standing as a neutral mediator and its partnership with the Taliban against ISKP.

“Russia’s primary concern is ISKP and it appears satisfied with the Taliban’s efforts to counter the group,” Abdul Sayed, a Sweden-based analyst specialising in armed groups and security dynamics in Afghanistan and Pakistan, told Al Jazeera.

Still, Russia has something earlier mediators did not. In July 2025, it became the only country to recognise the Taliban government.

Taimur Khan said that could give Moscow another source of influence.

“The Taliban authorities’ interest in preserving that recognition and expanding cooperation with Moscow could give Russia additional influence in seeking action against the TTP and other terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan,” he said.

In May, the two sides signed an unpublished military-technical agreement covering, according to Kabulov, the repair and maintenance of equipment the Taliban already hold, mostly Soviet and Russian-made.

Three days after the signing, the Taliban’s Defence Minister, Mohammad Yaqoob, said Pakistan would soon no longer dare to launch strikes.

On June 9 and 10, Pakistani aircraft struck Kunar, Khost and Paktika provinces, killing 13 civilians, according to the Afghan government.

“Russia has greater access to the Taliban than any other major power, but its actual leverage is considerably more limited than is often assumed,” analyst Gusseinov said.

Sayed said senior Taliban leaders continued visiting Russia and India as fighting escalated, seemingly signalling they could offset Pakistan’s military superiority through new alignments.

“While the military and political significance of these ties remains unclear, the Taliban present such diplomatic developments to the Afghan public, particularly their supporters, as political achievements that reinforce their image of strength,” he said.

Pakistan chairs the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) for 2026-27 and will host the 10-member bloc’s summit in Islamabad next year.

The Taliban were not invited to this year’s summit in Bishkek , where members called for an inclusive government in Kabul.

On July 16, then-Foreign Office spokesperson Tahir Andrabi said Afghanistan first needed diplomatic relations with member states, when asked whether Pakistan was blocking its inclusion in the SCO.

In September, Tirmizi, the Pakistani envoy in Moscow, said he did not see full SCO membership for Afghanistan as an option under the current Taliban government.

“The chairmanship strengthens Moscow’s reasons to invest in its relationship with Pakistan and manage differences over Afghanistan constructively,” Taimur Khan said.

The Foreign Office did not answer Al Jazeera’s questions about whether the Taliban would be invited next year.

“I cannot recall an instance where Kabul has explicitly requested Moscow to mediate between the two countries,” Bahiss said. “Nevertheless, Kabul’s repeated calls for diplomacy and its relatively close relations with Russia suggest that it would likely welcome Russian mediation if Moscow offered to play such a role.”

articles.title: How Israeli firm’s ‘zero-click’ malware attack poses global security risk
articles.summary: A new ‘zero-click’ hack uses ads to target victims without any action needed on their part.
articles.body:
Just visiting a page or refreshing an app can be enough to fall victim to a malware attack in which your personal data is stolen from a laptop or phone, researchers have found. You are not even required to “click” on anything.

An Israeli spyware firm has been found to be behind the first-known instance of “zero-click” targeted advertising in which fraudsters or spies can steal private data and send it to external servers, with Al Jazeera journalists among the victims.

In June 2025, 45 devices used by Al Jazeera staff – including several who reported on sensitive subjects – were targeted with spyware which installed itself without the need to open or download any files.

An investigation by the Canada-based academic research unit Citizen Lab, prompted by Al Jazeera’s initial internal probe into the issue, discovered that the Israeli company Candiru was behind the attacks.

Analysts say the findings are “incredibly concerning”, as they confirm the existence of a new global security threat. “We knew we were headed in this direction and now it is out in the public,” Remesh Srinivasan, professor of information studies at the University of California in Los Angeles, US, told Al Jazeera.

“This is the next level, because people are being microtargeted,” he said. “This is the point we’ve come to when it comes to surveillance.”

Al Jazeera’s in-house technology team first discovered unusual patterns on devices used by some journalists in 2024. Analysis of network logs provided to the Citizen Lab by Al Jazeera in 2025 provided a clear temporal signature of how the attack was executed.

Malicious advertisements were bought by Discover-Tech, an Israeli company presenting itself as a legitimate advertising firm, but which actually operates as a facilitator for mercenary spyware partners.

Its advertisement network identified Al Jazeera staff, then quietly redirected them to an infected server belonging to Candiru. The spyware firm was blacklisted by the US government in 2021, when Citizen Lab found it was responsible for the illegal hacking and surveillance of at least 100 activists , journalists and political activists across 10 countries.

Al Jazeera Media Network has condemned the targeting of its staff members’ devices and called for those responsible to be held accountable.

Cybersecurity analyst and author Eddy Willems said the advertisements used automatically infect devices the moment they pop up on the screen, but there is an important technical nuance. “Executing code inside the browser does not automatically give an attacker full control over the computer,” Willems told Al Jazeera.

“To escape the browser’s isolated environment – the ‘sandbox’ – the attacker may need a second vulnerability,” Willems said, adding that an advanced spyware operation can combine several vulnerabilities.

“The attacker attempts to exploit vulnerabilities to bypass security boundaries. This is precisely what makes this type of attack so dangerous,” the analyst said.

Once the device is infected, the malicious software is designed to collect a wide range of sensitive data, including files, documents, and browser data such as cookies, bookmarks, and saved credentials.

It can also capture keystrokes, take screenshots, record microphone and webcam input, and extract emails and messages from popular communication platforms. To avoid triggering security mechanisms, the spyware often uses encrypted communication channels and breaks up stolen data into smaller chunks sent over time.

Analysts say Citizen Lab’s findings point to the escalation of an existing threat, which expands the scale and reach of traditional cyberattacks and makes them much harder to detect.

While “zero-click” attacks are not completely new, the findings outline a new technique through which online advertisements are used as a route to infection.

Stephen O’Shaughnessy, a lecturer in cybersecurity at the TU Dublin Blanchardstown campus in Ireland, explained that when a user opens a website or app, an automated auction sells the advertisement space in a fraction of a second. That auction shares data about the victim, including the device ID, IP address, rough location and the app or site they are on.

“Discover-Tech posed as an ordinary advertiser, used that data to find their target and win the auction for that person’s screen,” O’Shaughnessy told Al Jazeera. “Anyone with a phone or browser that shows ads can be reached, without the attacker needing their phone number or email.”

“Because no message or link is involved, there is almost nothing for the victim to notice,” he added.

Discover-Tech appeared on lists of “certified” and “approved” vendors maintained by Google and advertising industry association IAB Europe, and has served advertisements via major networks such as Google, Yandex and Beeswax.

In its report, Citizen Lab said this illustrates the structural flaws in the online advertising system, which essentially failed to detect or prevent the abuse.

Discover-Tech advertisements have popped up on devices used by personnel in national-security-sensitive networks around the world, including those of various ministries of defence, armed forces, national cyber agencies, intergovernmental organisations and media outlets, Citizen Lab found.

The research unit said these advertisements have also appeared on networks used by the United Nations, NATO, the European Parliament, the European Commission and the Council of the European Union’s General Secretariat.

Government networks have also been targeted in at least 24 countries, including the United States, Italy, Denmark, Norway, Australia, Russia, Mexico and Israel itself. Networks of media organisations have also been targeted, mainly in Australia, Denmark and Sweden, according to Citizen Lab.

In a separate report, New York-based advertising security firm Confiant said its own investigations had found that some of Discover-Tech’s advertisements also appeared in critical networks used by the Pentagon, the United Nations International Atomic Energy Agency and the International Criminal Court.

O’Shaughnessy said infection has not been confirmed there – only profiling of users. “But that alone is concerning, he said. “The ad system was built to send code from strangers to billions of screens with pinpoint targeting. Almost nobody was watching it from a security angle.”

The analyst said the risk remains low for most people as these attacks are expensive and aimed at specific targets. “For individuals at high risk, like journalists and officials, the best first defence is to install an ad blocker, switch off their advertising ID through their phone’s privacy settings, keep everything updated, and turn on Lockdown Mode or Android’s Advanced Protection,” he said.

Precautions also need to be taken within the industry and at government level. “To combat this, the ad industry needs to properly vet who’s buying ads,” O’Shaughnessy said, while “regulators need to stop personal data being sprayed out to thousands of unknown bidders in every auction.”

articles.title: In 2013, Oprah Winfrey gave $12 million to a Smithsonian museum; 13 years later, its 350-seat theatre bearing her name continues hosting public conversations about Black history and culture
articles.summary: A $12 million donation from Oprah Winfrey to the Smithsonian Institution continues to support public discussions about African American history and
articles.body: A $12 million donation from Oprah Winfrey to the Smithsonian Institution continues to support public discussions about African American history and culture in the nation's capital. The Smithsonian Institution announced the donation in June 2013. The money supported fundraising for the National Museum of African American History and Culture. Along with an earlier gift of $1 million made in 2007, Winfrey's total contribution reached $13 million. This made her the largest individual donor to the museum during its development. To recognize her support, the Smithsonian named the building's 350-seat performance space the Oprah Winfrey Theater. Located below ground, the theater hosts live performances, academic talks, film screenings and public debates in Washington, DC.A landmark contribution to building costsWinfrey joined the museum's advisory council in 2004. She worked with civic leaders, legal experts and cultural figures to help guide the institution's planning and development. Her $12 million pledge in 2013 gave an important boost to a $500 million fundraising campaign. Half of the money was expected to come from federal funding approved by Congress, while the other half would come from private donations.When the donation was announced, Winfrey spoke about her commitment to preserving Black history for future generations."I am so proud of African American history and its contributions to our nation as a whole," Winfrey stated in an official Smithsonian Institution press release. "I am deeply appreciative of those who paved the path for me and all who follow in their footsteps. By investing in this museum, I want to help ensure that we both honor and preserve our culture and history, so that the stories of who we are will live on for generations to come."Lonnie G. Bunch III, the museum's founding director, spoke about the wider educational value of Winfrey's donation."We are inspired and profoundly grateful for Ms. Winfrey's generosity at this important time," Bunch said in the Smithsonian statement. "Her gifts will forever be associated with harnessing the power of art and creative expression to build bridges between cultures and enrich people's lives. Programming at the Oprah Winfrey Theater will mirror the museum's commitment to use African American history and culture as a lens to see what it means to be an American and to help all Americans remember."Wayne Clough, who was Secretary of the Smithsonian Institution during the fundraising campaign, said Winfrey's support matched the theater's cultural purpose."At its heart, the National Museum of African American History and Culture is a showcase for a richer, fuller picture of the American experience," Clough said in the 2013 release. "The Oprah Winfrey Theater will bring untold stories alive through films, live performances, artistic expression and public dialogue."Architectural design and underground locationThe National Museum of African American History and Culture officially began construction in February 2012 on a five-acre site next to the Washington Monument. The 400,000-square-foot building was designed by Freelon Adjaye Bond/SmithGroupJJR, a team made up of four leading design firms.According to design fact sheets released by the Smithsonian Institution, the architectural firm Davis Brody Bond was responsible for designing the Oprah Winfrey Theater and the nearby underground History Galleries. Building 60 per cent of the museum below ground created major engineering challenges during the four-year construction project.The Oprah Winfrey Theater is located on Concourse 0. This underground level also contains an atrium, a quiet court for reflection, a special exhibitions gallery and a dining area. Above ground, the museum's main exterior feature is the "Corona". This three-level structure takes inspiration from traditional Yoruba wooden columns from West Africa. It is covered with 3,600 bronze-coloured cast-aluminium panels.The theater opened to the public with the rest of the museum during an official dedication ceremony on 24 September 2016.Ongoing public programming and cultural dialogueThe 350-seat theater remains one of the largest working spaces inside the museum. It regularly welcomes historians, filmmakers, authors, musicians and policy advocates for public discussions.Events held at the theater, including the "Historically Speaking" symposium series, explore topics such as building the museum's collections, preserving historical records, civil rights history and modern cultural research. Through live presentations and digital broadcasts from the stage, the theater continues to serve its original purpose as a national platform for African American voices and perspectives.You use AI every day. articles.title: Qatar announces ‘massive’ solar plant project in Lebanon
articles.summary: Sheikh Mohammed also discussed Israeli ‘violations’ in Lebanese territory with Prime Minister Nawaf Salam.
articles.body:
Qatar’s prime minister has announced plans to set up what he described as a “massive” solar plant in Lebanon to help ease its energy crisis .

Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani made the announcement during his visit to Beirut on Friday, after meeting his Lebanese counterpart, Nawaf Salam.

“We have agreed to establish a comprehensive framework for cooperation in the energy sector and to present viable solutions,” Sheikh Mohammed said.

QatarEnergy has reached an agreement with French company TotalEnergies to jointly develop a solar power plant in Lebanon as an initial project.

The aim is to develop a major investment project “that would benefit the Lebanese economy, as well as the Qatari companies and entities participating in it”, he added.

Prime Minister Salam said he would put the plans for Lebanon’s electricity sector to the Lebanese Cabinet soon.

“The Qatari side will fund, implement and activate the project without any cost on the Lebanese state,” Lebanon’s leader said, adding that such a move is important because of the country’s financial crisis.

Lebanon’s state electricity company is one of the biggest sources of debt, haemorrhaging about $40bn over past decades with a bloated workforce and outdated infrastructure. The company provides only a few hours of electricity a day and the state, until a year ago, took advances from the Central Bank when diesel fuel ran out.

Sheikh Mohammed said Doha stands in “solidarity with the Lebanese people” and the entire region “in this dire hour”. Lebanon has been struggling with multiple energy crises in recent years and the situation has been compounded by the country’s financial collapse and Israel’s ongoing assault .

Earlier in the day, the Qatari PM also met Lebanon’s president and parliament speaker.

Among the topics discussed was the situation in southern Lebanon, where Israel continues its assault, capturing dozens of towns and villages.

Sheikh Mohammed said “Israeli violations within the Lebanese territories” were a large part of his talks.

He said that Israel should withdraw from Lebanon and cease its attacks, adding that Qatar is working in coordination with the United States to help lay the groundwork for future reconstruction in southern Lebanon to allow displaced people to return to their homes.

Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon have continued despite a ceasefire agreed in June. Under the agreement brokered by the US, the Lebanese government is to disarm Iran-backed Hezbollah. In return, Israeli forces will gradually withdraw from southern areas that they occupy. However, Hezbollah is not part of the agreement and has refused to disarm until Israel withdraws from the country.

Lebanese authorities say Israeli attacks have killed more than 4,300 people in the country since March. About 1.2 million people were also displaced in Lebanon at the height of the war.

Although most have returned home since the June ceasefire, more than 300,000 people remain displaced, according to the International Organization for Migration.

Lebanon’s PM Salam thanked Qatar for its “continuous” support during some of Lebanon’s “darkest hours”.

articles.title: Hibaldstow man jailed for sex with dead woman
articles.summary: Stephen Sellars, 62, was interrupted by the woman's son and nephew, a court hears.
articles.body:
A man has been jailed for having sex with a dead body.

Stephen Sellars, 62, of Hibaldstow, North Lincolnshire, was interrupted by the woman's son and nephew as he carried out the act in her home.

On Friday, Sellars was sentenced to 16 months' imprisonment at Hull Crown Court. He pleaded guilty to the offence of sexual penetration of a corpse at an earlier hearing.

In a statement read to the court, the victim's son said the incident had a "massive impact" on him and described the offence as "unimaginable" and that "nothing could ever justify it".

Passing sentence, Judge John Thackray KC said if the offence had taken place "less than a month later" he would have been able to sentence Sellars to a maximum of seven years in prison due to a law change.

As it stood, the judge said he could only impose a maximum sentence of two years, which he reduced due to his early guilty plea.

Prosecutor Rachel Scott said the woman had died at home after being diagnosed with cancer eight weeks earlier.

The court heard the victim was a "very proud woman" and they had tried to "preserve her dignity" throughout her illness.

Scott said Sellars had been left alone with the victim at the property for about 15 minutes.

It was on return to the house that the victim's son and nephew caught Sellars committing the offence.

He then got dressed and "ran out of the property", said Scott.

In text messages shared between the victim's son and Sellars, the defendant said he "was smashed" and "I didn't know what came over me".

Scott told the court that Sellars had said to officers: "It was obvious what was going to happen, wasn't it?"

In interview, Sellars denied the offence.

Scott said there were a number of aggravating features to the case, pointing out the crime took place in the presence of the woman's family, in her own home, and there was "a significant abuse of trust".

In addition, the barrister said there was "some degree of planning" after Sellars bolted a gate, locked the door, and shut the curtains to carry out the offence.

Ben Donnell, mitigating, said Sellars had not committed an offence since 1988, and had never committed a sexual offence.

He said he had worked as a lorry driver and was a "good employee".

Donnell admitted it was a "tall ask" but asked the judge whether Sellars' sentence could be suspended and served in the community.

Sentencing, Thackray said it was a "clearly planned attack", which left her son feeling "numb and betrayed", and said he "doesn't think he will ever fully recover" from what happened.

The judge also imposed a five-year sexual harm prevention order on Sellars and a restraining order in respect of the victim's son and nephew.
