articles.title: Pope Leo to make public appearance Sunday, first since cancer surgery
articles.summary: After undergoing surgery this week, pope can now ‘carry out normal activities with full independence’, say doctors.
articles.body:
Pope Leo XIV is making steady progress at the hospital after undergoing lung surgery earlier this week, according to his doctors, as the Vatican says he plans to appear before the public on Sunday.

The 71-year-old Catholic leader, who has been diagnosed with lung cancer, underwent an operation to remove part of his right lung on Tuesday.

He is now able to “carry out normal daily activities with full independence”, his doctors said in a medical update on Friday.

A blood test and chest X-ray earlier in the day confirmed his “steady improvement”, added the medical bulletin.

The update came as the Vatican shared the first images of Leo since his surgery, showing him celebrating mass and standing unaided in the Rome hospital where he is recovering.

The Vatican said Leo will deliver a traditional noontime prayer on Sunday, marking his first public appearance since the operation.

Preparations are also going ahead for his planned trip to South America in November, The Holy See added.

Leo’s cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy.

The Vatican did ⁠not say on Friday when the pontiff might be discharged from hospital, but previously indicated his recovery would take about a week.

The pope’s doctors have said his surgery was completed successfully, without complications. They have not yet disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis.

Chicago Cardinal Blase Cupich, seen as a close ally of ‌Leo, said he had been shocked by news of the cancer diagnosis.

He told Catholic magazine America he thought Leo had “downplayed” his health issue on Sunday, when the pope announced he needed surgery for a small, well-contained growth on his lung.

“When I heard they took ‌out ‌part of the lobe of the lung and that it was malignant, that was more shocking and more concerning,” said Cupich. “I think people are very concerned and even worried about this but hoping for the best.”

Leo is due to ⁠visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from November 6 to 17. Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori had speculated that the trip might have to be delayed, ‌but in a sign that preparations were carrying on as normal, the Vatican released a list of journalists admitted to ‌cover ‌the visit.

Work on the trip is “going forward”, said a Vatican spokesman.

Leo also continued to work from the hospital on Friday, including speaking by phone with Russian President Vladimir Putin. During the call, the pope pushed for a ceasefire to allow aid and food into the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Vatican said.

articles.title: Man who confronted Oregon elementary school gunman identified by brother
articles.summary: Kaylub Giamanco was driving home from lunch Thursday afternoon when he heard gunshots and saw a gunman entering the Oregon elementary school his two young daughters attend.
articles.body: Kaylub Giamanco was driving home from lunch Thursday afternoon when he heard gunshots and saw a gunman entering the Oregon elementary school his two young daughters attend. The 36-year-old carpenter ran into the school and killed the teenage suspect. Kyle Giamanco identified his brother as the bystander and recounted to NBC News on Friday what he was told happened. Officials have not named the community member, but said the person’s actions prevented further loss at Silver Rail Elementary School. Kyle Giamanco said his brother told him he was headed home after grabbing a bite to eat when he saw the gunman entering the school. Police have said that the suspect, identified by three senior law enforcement officials as John J. Griffin, 16, gained entry to the building by firing through locked doors. Two of the officials said the gun used in the shooting was purchased by the suspect’s mother around the time of his birthday in August. Kyle Giamanco said his brother has a concealed-weapon permit “and decided to go in after” the shooter. Kyle Giamanco and several parents told NBC News that the shooting happened in a special education room. A teacher and three children, ages 5, 8 and 11, were killed. Two other people, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were critically injured at the Bend, Oregon, school. Kyle Giamanco said his brother is a hero, but said Kaylub Giamanco does not want to speak out right now because he feels guilty that he could not save more children. Kaylub Giamanco wasn’t the only person to try to stop the gunman. The first 911 call was placed by a person who reported that the gunman shot at his vehicle. That call and the dozens of others that police said were placed to 911 reporting that a gunman had entered the school enabled police to arrive on scene just three minutes after the first call, according to police. Justin Penfield said his son is in kindergarten and when he got to the school, the class was already outside. As he walked back to his car with his son, Penfield said he saw a man standing next to a pickup truck with “seven or eight gunshot holes in his truck.” Penfield said the man told him that he was driving back from lunch when he saw someone throw what appeared to be a shotgun over the fence and then jump into the school’s playground. The man said he yelled to ask the guy what he was doing, and the person opened fire on his truck, Penfield said, recounting his conversation with the man. According to Penfield, the man said he sped off and called 911. The names of those killed and injured have not been released. One parent recalled getting an automated phone call from the school about a lockdown, followed by a text message from her son saying that there had been a shooting. “Mom there was a school shooting we’re ok tho,” the fifth grader wrote. Jenn Johnston said she and her husband rushed to the school but were rerouted to a nearby church. They waited hours with few updates from police or school officials before she was reunited with her son. “My son came running to me in tears,” she said.

articles.title: US tells election officials to guard against AI-powered cyber threats ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: The FBI and the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have warned election officials, candidates and the American public to remain
articles.body: The FBI and the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) have warned election officials, candidates and the American public to remain alert to AI-powered cyber threats ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, warning that hackers could use convincing fake emails and text messages to steal sensitive information.In an alert issued on Friday, the agencies said cybercriminals could target election officials, candidates and political organisations with fraudulent messages designed to obtain passwords and other sensitive data, according to Reuters.“Election officials, candidates, and their political organizations are attractive targets to malicious cyber criminals,” the alert said.The advisory also warned that advances in artificial intelligence could make phishing attempts more convincing. The alert referred to “super intelligence”, a term endorsed by US President Donald Trump, and said the technology was helping hackers improve fraudulent emails and text messages to make them appear more authentic, Reuters reported.The warning comes amid a separate investigation into suspicious mailings sent to election officials and lawmakers ahead of the midterm polls.The FBI and the US Postal Inspection Service, the law enforcement arm of the US Postal Service, said on Thursday they were investigating letters sent to state election officials and lawmakers’ offices. Some of the letters reportedly contained an unidentified substance.The investigation comes less than three weeks before the November 3 elections, which will determine control of the US Congress. The Postal Service is also preparing to process millions of mail-in ballots.Spokespersons for Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer and Democratic senators Alex Padilla of California and Chris Murphy of Connecticut said the Postal Service had intercepted letters containing a suspicious substance that were addressed to their offices, Reuters reported.“This incident is a stark reminder of the very real dangers facing those who serve the public and who help administer our elections,” Padilla said in a statement.The US House of Representatives sergeant at arms, the chamber’s chief law enforcement officer, also informed staff that some public officials had received letters containing suspicious white powder.Brendan Donahue, a deputy chief inspector with the US Postal Inspection Service, said some suspicious letters had been intercepted and the investigation was continuing.“We are committed to protecting our nation's election officials from threatening and dangerous mail. Any threat or attack on an election official is unacceptable,” Donahue told reporters.The National Association of Secretaries of State and the National Association of State Election Directors said on Wednesday that a series of suspicious letters had been sent to state election offices. Letters addressed to election offices in Pennsylvania, Ohio and Idaho were intercepted before delivery, Reuters reported.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Russia strikes 9 Ukrainian regions as new report shows spike in civilian casualties
articles.summary: Russian strikes across nine regions of Ukraine disrupted electricity supplies to hundreds of thousands of households and injured at least 15 people,
articles.body: Russian strikes across nine regions of Ukraine disrupted electricity supplies to hundreds of thousands of households and injured at least 15 people, officials said on Friday. The attacks came as a new report revealed a sharp rise in civilian casualties since Russia launched its invasion.The latest wave of aerial attacks on civilian infrastructure has heightened concerns that worsening relations between Kyiv and Washington could leave Ukraine more vulnerable to Russia’s intensifying assault as winter approaches.Russia has repeatedly targeted Ukraine’s power infrastructure ahead of winter, seeking to weaken public morale by disrupting heating and water supplies. Ukrainian officials have warned that Moscow is stockpiling ballistic missiles for further attacks in the coming months.On Thursday, Ukraine ended a short-lived truce covering energy infrastructure, saying Moscow had failed to honour the arrangement despite US President Donald Trump’s call for a ceasefire, according to AP.Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy attended a summit of European union leaders in Brussels on Friday, where he received applause from leaders who share his concerns over Russian aggression and Moscow’s broader ambitions in Europe. The leaders pledged continued support for Ukraine and called on Washington to increase pressure on Russian president Vladimir Putin.Trump-Zelenskyy tensions raise concerns over US supportRelations between Trump and Zelenskyy came under renewed scrutiny after the two leaders exchanged sharp public remarks, fuelling uncertainty in Ukraine and across Europe.On Thursday, Zelenskyy said he felt betrayed by the American president. Trump, meanwhile, openly criticised the Ukrainian leader during an interview with Newsmax, saying, “Zelenskyy is not a good guy for us to deal with.”Speaking ahead of the EU summit, Zelenskyy thanked the 27-member bloc for standing by Ukraine, describing its leaders as “real leaders”.“We want to end this war as (quickly) as possible,” Zelenskyy told reporters in English. “We don’t see now signals from (the) Russian side that they are ready for this, to end this war. That’s why we have to prepare for the winter.”The growing rift has raised fears that Washington could further reduce its support for Ukraine’s war effort.Ukraine faces shortages of Patriot missilesUkraine continues to face a severe shortage of US-made Patriot air defence missiles, which are essential for intercepting Russia’s destructive ballistic missile attacks. Zelenskyy has repeatedly urged Washington to supply additional systems and ammunition.Speaking in Brussels, he said Ukraine had received limited numbers of patriot interceptors in recent months. Some were purchased from the United States by European countries for Kyiv, while others came from the existing stockpiles of countries around the world.Zelenskyy also expressed concern over disruptions to Western intelligence-sharing arrangements and sudden speed restrictions affecting Starshield, the military-grade version of spaceX’s starlink satellite internet service. The technology plays a crucial role in Ukraine’s drone operations and military communications.Restrictions that reduced the speed of Ukrainian drone interceptors to 70 kph (43 mph) came as a “dangerous and unpleasant surprise”, he said. However, he added that higher speeds needed to intercept Russian jet-powered drones travelling at more than 400 kph (250 mph) were being restored.“Have they returned to previous speed limits? No. But is it coming back? Yes,” Zelenskyy told a news conference.He also criticised Trump’s diesel deal with Russia, despite international efforts to impose sanctions and isolate Moscow diplomatically over its invasion of Ukraine. Although Trump had promised to end the war swiftly, Ukrainian officials have accused him of pressuring Kyiv to surrender territory to Russia.“There are so many people with good hearts in America, who sincerely want evil to lose and Ukraine to stand strong,” Zelenskyy told the EU summit. “And at the end of the day, the American people will have their say.”Zelenskyy seeks €79 billion in European assistanceThe European Union is working to persuade Washington to maintain its backing for Ukraine, the bloc’s foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, said.“We are trying to convince also our American partners that if we want to end this war, then we have to squeeze the aggressor,” Kallas said. “With our American allies it’s very difficult at the moment.”Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin, whose country currently holds the EU’s rotating presidency, said there was widespread concern across Europe over the latest developments in Ukraine.Zelenskyy told European leaders that the war would cost Ukraine 155 billion euros ($174 billion) next year. He said the country would require at least 70 billion euros ($79 billion) in assistance from Europe.UN reports 85% rise in civilian casualtiesRussian attacks have increasingly targeted civilian infrastructure, including residential buildings, public transport networks, cargo vessels, data centres and grocery stores, alongside the country’s electricity grid.The United nations human rights office in Kyiv said Ukrainian civilians were bearing a growing toll from the intensifying attacks in a monthly report released on Friday.At least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in September, representing an 85% increase in casualties compared with the same month last year, the report said. It added that Russian attacks during October had already killed dozens more civilians, including children.“The first two weeks of October were among the deadliest periods for civilians in years,” said Danielle Bell, head of the UN office.Ukrainian drone strikes disrupt Russian air travelUkraine has also continued its campaign against Russia using domestically developed long-range drones.Russia’s defence ministry said on Friday that its air defence systems had intercepted 644 Ukrainian drones overnight across several Russian regions, the illegally annexed Crimean Peninsula and the Black sea.The overnight restrictions imposed on aviation operations delayed more than 200 flights departing from four Moscow airports, Russian news agency interfax reported.St Petersburg airport also experienced disruptions, with local media reporting that another 46 flights were delayed or cancelled.You use AI every day. articles.title: US records 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows
articles.summary: The CDC reports 451 hospitalisations nationwide as health officials expand vaccination efforts.
articles.body:
The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has recorded 4,410 measles cases so far in 2026, an increase of 330 in a week, and has dispatched an investigator to the state of Pennsylvania to help contain the country’s largest outbreak.

CDC figures also show 451 measles-related hospitalisations nationwide this year. Children and teenagers aged five to 19 account for 42 percent of cases, followed by adults aged 20 and older, who make up 41 percent. Seventeen percent of cases were among children under the age of five.

Pennsylvania reported 1,222 cases across 42 counties as of Wednesday, including 86 new infections since October 9, according to the state health department. The outbreak has led to 225 hospitalisations and five confirmed measles-associated deaths. State officials are actively investigating a sixth reported death.

The CDC is sending a so-called “disease detective” from its Epidemic Intelligence Service to work with state health officials on the Pennsylvania outbreak. The deployment follows Pennsylvania’s request for federal assistance, known as an Epi-Aid .

Pennsylvania has expanded vaccination efforts in affected communities. State health centre staff have administered more than 5,900 measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine doses at 202 pop-up clinics since the outbreak began in late April.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on October 5 as measles cases rose in nearby Pennsylvania. The order is effective until November 4 and expands the number of healthcare professionals authorised to administer vaccines and allows nurses greater flexibility to order measles testing.

Measles vaccination coverage among US kindergarteners fell from 95.2 percent in the 2019–2020 school year to 92.4 percent in 2025–2026, according to data from the CDC. The agency estimates that about 280,000 kindergarteners are at risk because of gaps in vaccination coverage.

articles.summary: Chatribari Durga Puja pandal in Guwahati will showcase Assam’s 14 indigenous tribal cultures, traditional attire, instruments, and two unique idols.
articles.body: Guwahati: The Chatribari Durga Puja committee pandal will showcase the traditions, attire and identities of Assam’s 14 indigenous tribal communities this year.Standing over 60 feet tall, the pandal will highlight the cultural diversity of communities, including the Rabha, Mising, Bodo, Koch-Rajbongshi, Deori, Tea Tribes and Kachari, among others. The project has a budget of around Rs 18 lakh.“One of the major attractions will be the display of original traditional attire representing the different indigenous communities. The theme, he added, would go beyond conventional decoration and allow visitors to learn about the cultural diversity that shapes Assam.By bringing different tribal identities together, the committee hopes to promote greater awareness, inclusivity and appreciation of the state’s indigenous traditions.“The opening has been planned for the sixth day of the festival during the evening hours,” he said.Artists have crafted two idols for the puja: a traditional clay idol and another made entirely of grains, pulses and spices. articles.title: BEMT sunscreens are starting to hit shelves in the U.S. — here’s what you should know
articles.summary: BEMT is the first newly approved sunscreen ingredient in over 25 years — I spoke to a dermatologist to find out why it’s worth trying.
articles.body: American sunscreens are finally getting a face lift — this June, the FDA added bemotrizinol (BEMT) to its list of approved sunscreen active ingredients, marking the first new addition in more than 25 years. The ingredient is already a staple in other countries, and is already a common ingredient in many popular Korean sunscreen formulas. Although this is the first new ingredient to be approved in decades, it likely won’t be the last — according to Dr. Hadley King, a board-certified dermatologist in New York City, this is “likely just the beginning of a broader conversation about sunscreen innovation in the U.S.” Keep reading for everything you need to know about BEMT, including which sunscreen formulas made with it are available now. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. What is BEMT? Bemotrizinol is a broad-spectrum chemical filter for ultraviolet (UV) rays that helps protect against both UVA and UVB radiation, according to King. Though it’s been used in products in European, Asian, and Australian markets for years, it was recently approved by the FDA as an active sunscreen ingredient in the U.S. — the first newly-approved ingredient in more than 25 years. Since sunscreen is under the FDA’s drug classification category, the ingredient had to go through a rigorous approval process before reaching shelves here. “This is a major milestone because it is the first new sunscreen active ingredient added to the FDA’s [over-the-counter] sunscreen monograph since the late 1990s,” says King. “For years, dermatologists have pointed out that American consumers had access to fewer UV filters than consumers in many other countries.” She believes the addition of BEMT represents a meaningful step toward updating and modernizing sunscreen formulas in the U.S., and encouraging new product innovation in sun protection. What are the benefits of BEMT? There are a number of reasons BEMT is an exciting sun care addition, says King. “One of its most notable characteristics is that it is highly photostable, meaning it does not significantly degrade when exposed to sunlight, allowing it to provide consistent UV protection throughout sun exposure,” she says. A few other BEMT benefits she notes include: Strong, broad-spectrum protection against UVA and UVB rays in a single filter.Unlike ingredients like avobenzone, which requires stabilization in the sun, it prevents breakdown in sunlight, says King.It has low skin absorption, which prevents ingredients from penetrating too deeply into your skin, allowing it to stay on the surface (where it’s most needed for sun protection).It can be used to create formulas that feel lightweight on the skin while still maintaining a high level of protection. The best BEMT sunscreens Although BEMT was very recently approved in the United States, brands are already updating old formulas and rolling out new ones that feature the ingredient. Below, I rounded up the best sunscreens with BEMT that are on the market right now, created by tried-and-true brands trusted by NBC Selected editors. This formula from viral Australian sunscreen brand Ultra Violette is made specifically for acne-prone skin — thanks to the new BEMT filter, the sunscreen is gentle, non-irritating, and has broad-spectrum protection, according to the brand. It has a soft matte finish that’s ideal for keeping greasiness at bay on oily skin, and includes pentavitin, a moisturizing blend of plant extracts that helps keep skin hydrated for up to 72 hours. The sunscreen’s packaging also includes a push-pump applicator that lets you control how much you’re using while keeping the rest safely sealed away from air exposure. Neutrogena is one of our favorite brands for moisturizers and sun care, and the brand has recently revamped some of its bestselling formulas to include the BEMT filter. This Clear Face sunscreen has a noncomedogenic formula that won’t clog your pores, and includes niacinamide and vitamin E to help calm sun irritation on your skin, according to Neutrogena. It’s fast absorbing and reviewers say it layers well under makeup and leaves no visible white cast. If you have dry to normal skin, this may be the formula for you. It includes a multi-peptide blend that supports the skin’s collagen production, and dries down invisibly, making it great for all skin tones, according to the brand. It has a non-greasy, dewy finish and is water-resistant for up to 80 minutes. La Roche-Posay’s Anthelios sunscreen is a longtime favorite of NBC Selected editors, myself included. The sunscreen absorbs quickly into the skin without leaving a white cast, and I love that it is hydrating without being greasy. The formula includes an antioxidant complex to protect against free radicals, according to the brand, and it has a milky texture that feels very lightweight on the skin.
